caption_draft: System boundary and the thirteen computed cross-engine feeds. Tier-0 feeds are identity arithmetic on permit-application fields and are retained in the sequential-review counterfactual; tier-1 and tier-2 feeds are severed; the tier-3 scale proxy is reported separately because severing it substitutes another application field. Grey lines: engine outputs normalized into the composite score. Excluded flows are listed at right.

Interconnection map of the ten impact dimensions. Numbered arrows are the fourteen pathways of the registry (thirteen computed cross-engine feeds sit behind them: four tier-0 identity feeds and nine severable feeds, of which eight are severed in the manuscript definition of sequential review); solid blue arrows are numerically wired engine-to-engine feeds or within-engine derivations, dashed arrows are qualitative pathways, line width scales with the number of sites (0–6) at which the pathway is numerically active (its severing changes an engine output).

Normalized impact profile of each site across the ten dimensions under balanced weights. Hatched bars are dimensions that hit the upper bound of their normalization range (v4: Saline health, 0-500 $M); Food is assessed where regional crop production is entered (all sites except Tucson).

(a) Composite Nexus Impact Score of the six sites under the five weighting presets. (b) Weighted contribution of each dimension to the balanced-weight score; a cell at 0.100 means the dimension is saturated (only Saline health in v4).

(a) Nexus Impact Score under each site's own weighting preset with full cross-engine propagation (coupled) versus sequential single-sector review, in which the tier-1 information feeds and the tier-2 regional-health feed are severed, and versus the legacy definition that also severs the tier-3 scale proxy; labels give the relative understatement. (b) Exact Shapley attribution of the coupled − sequential gap to each severable feed (sum over feeds equals the gap). R = energy, H = health, CM = community, SC = supply chain, L = land, EW = e-waste, F = food, W = water, UHI = heat island.

Threshold screening of the six sites against the 21 rules of the compliance engine (6 regulatory, 15 advisory; the WHO noise guideline is advisory in v4). Cells show pass/warn/fail with the value-to-threshold ratio for exceedances.
One-at-a-time sensitivity of the site-preset Nexus Impact Score to a ±20 % change in each input; the ten most influential inputs per site are shown.

Uncertainty propagation. (a) Distribution of the site-preset Nexus Impact Score across 10,000 joint perturbations of all numeric inputs (design ±10 %, regional context ±25 %, socio-economic ±20 %, triangular). (b) Rank probability of each site under balanced weights. (c) Probability that each screening rule returns fail.

Change in the site-preset Nexus Impact Score produced by each mitigation intervention (a) and package (b); blue = improvement, red = deterioration. v4: recycled water reaches the freshwater withdrawal and basin-stress terms, extended server life the embodied intensity, and 90 % renewables acts only through the additionally procured share (Scope 2 and the grid-attributable health burden); the mitigation simulator resolves the same effective inputs (auto EWIF, power mix) as the baseline. Intended for the supplementary information.
Annual PM2.5 and NOx attributable to on-site backup/prime generation versus the fossil share of grid supply at each site (log scale); the ratio grid ÷ on-site is annotated.

Cascade test: all inputs held at preset values while IT load is scaled 0.5–3×. (a) Composite score under balanced weights, (b) log-elasticity of key engine outputs at 2× (1.00 = proportional; 0 = no response).

Dimension-level cascade: normalized scores of the eight responsive dimensions as IT load is scaled 0.5–3× with all other inputs fixed (dashed line = preset value). Food and land do not respond because their inputs are independent of IT load; e-waste falls with scale because the embodied intensity divides a fixed server fleet by IT MW.
Robustness of the balanced-weight Nexus Impact Score (cell value) and of the dominant dimension (cell label) to the normalization ranges applied to the same raw engine outputs.

Weight-robustness of the composite score: 5,000 weight vectors drawn uniformly on the ten-dimension simplex, applied to fixed baseline engine outputs. (a) Score range per site with the probability of ranking first. (b) Rank probabilities.

Supplementary: cumulative regional multipliers (ratio of cumulative existing + planned + proposed facilities to the single facility) from the cumulative engine's heuristic stacking rules (log colour scale). Illustrative screening output; multipliers are not calibrated.

Supplementary: climate-hazard exposure of the six sites: (a) eight hazard scores from the climate-risk engine (surface-water flooding unscored because no preset supplies annual rainfall), (b) weighted composite; the MODERATE band starts above 0.40; Tucson (0.41) is the only site above it.

Sensitivity of the population-weighted annual PM2.5 increment from the on-site generators (long-term Gaussian with Briggs rural dispersion, integrated over the 0–1, 1–5 and 5–10 km population rings, 10 m release height) to stability class and wind speed. No combination reaches the 2024 NAAQS annual standard (9 µg/m³) on the increment alone (cells would be outlined if one did); the v3 centreline-at-1-km metric gave 1–15 µg/m³ at the same presets. Preset defaults are class D at 3.5 m/s.

(a) Relative understatement of the site-preset Nexus Impact Score by sequential review under four operational definitions of which cross-engine feeds a sector-by-sector review lacks. (b) Exact Shapley attribution of the all-nine gap to the three feed tiers.

Correlation structure of the ten normalized dimensions: (a) across the six sites, (b) within each site across the Monte Carlo draws, averaged over sites. Blank cells: dimension constant (saturated) or not assessed.

Global sensitivity of the site-preset Nexus Impact Score: first-order and total-order Sobol indices (Saltelli design with centred outputs, 2,048 base samples, 123,000–131,000 model evaluations per site, same input distributions as the Monte Carlo analysis); ten most influential inputs per site by total-order index.

Sensitivity of the overall screening verdict to rule assumptions re-evaluated on the same engine outputs: the shipped v4 rules (metric-tonne thresholds, 500 h/yr potential-to-emit basis for emergency engines, AP-42 formaldehyde factors, WHO noise advisory, NAAQS on background + increment) versus the legacy v3 rules and single-assumption variants.
